entrance: Walk straight through without breaking stride
arrive: You are still walking out of the last verse's scene, mouth open, mid-sentence, and you simply keep going: same pace, same direction, not even a pause, straight into this scene where the three address pegs are already waiting. The ground of the last scene runs on under you; you never glanced down to see where one ended and the other began.
decode: Never stopped, never paused, still mid-sentence = this verse is joined straight onto the one before: And.
contrast: The open entrance has no walk at all (you are already standing there with nothing behind you); And is always caught mid-step with the previous scene still at your back.
example: Genesis 1:3 — you walk on out of 1:2 without breaking stride, still talking, and the three pegs are already there with a voice already speaking: And God said.
clear: A mid-stride crossing is a manner of arriving, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and no road, foot or feet are drawn (stride is the motion, not a peg).

entrance: Back in, pointing at last scene
arrive: You come in backwards, eyes fixed on the scene you just left, jabbing a finger at it the whole way: 'Because of THAT.' You do not turn round until you are fully inside among the pegs, and even then you keep glancing back over your shoulder at it.
decode: Backing in while pointing at what was just said = you are giving the reason for it: For (because).
contrast: So is shoved in from behind and stumbles forward facing away from the last scene; For walks in backwards facing it and pointing, and nobody pushed.
example: John 3:16 — you back into the scene, finger jabbed at 3:15, explaining it: For God so.
clear: Backing in is a posture of arrival, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and nothing from the peg table.

entrance: Skid to a halt and U-turn
arrive: You march in one way, fully committed, then screech to a stop, spin a half-turn on the spot, and stride in the exact opposite direction into the scene. The three pegs watch you arrive facing the way nobody expected.
decode: Arriving the opposite way from the way you set out = the reverse of what was expected: But.
contrast: For also faces backwards, but For backs in steadily and points; But skids, spins hard and marches off the opposite way with no pointing at all.
example: Isaiah 40:31 — you were marching along with 40:30, you skid, spin, and stride into the scene the opposite way: But they that.
clear: A skid and U-turn is pure motion, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and no road, foot or feet are drawn.

entrance: Fixed stare, straight to one thing
arrive: You cross in with your stare already fixed: everything else in the scene drains to grey and you walk dead straight, unblinking, to the one thing you came for, and stop right in front of it. You never look at anything else, because there is only the one.
decode: A stare fixed on one particular thing and nothing else = this one in particular: The.
contrast: Then steps in on its turn after someone else has left; The ignores everyone else entirely and homes in on the single thing.
example: Psalm 23:1 — you cross in with everything greyed out but one presence, shown as glory, and walk dead straight to it: The LORD is.
clear: A locked stare and a straight walk are a manner of arriving, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and nothing from the peg table.

entrance: Step in next, on your turn
arrive: The last scene's actor finishes, bows, and walks off; there is one clear beat of empty silence, and only then do you step forward into the space they left, exactly on your turn. Not with them, not before them: after.
decode: One finishes, a beat, then the next steps in = what comes next in order: Then.
contrast: The has you homing in on one thing with nobody leaving; Then is always someone finishing first and you stepping in after the gap (and unlike And, there IS a gap).
example: Matthew 4:1 — the scene of 3:17 finishes and clears, a beat, and you step in as the next in turn: Then was Jesus.
clear: Stepping in after a beat is timing and motion, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and nothing from the peg table.

entrance: Stride in centre-stage, thumping your chest
arrive: You come in dead centre, chest out, one fist thumping your own breastbone — 'ME' — and the whole scene is seen from behind your own eyes. You are not watching anyone; you are the one it is happening to.
decode: Thumping your own chest and seeing it all from your own eyes = the speaker is yourself: I.
contrast: He edges in at the side and watches someone else; I barges in centre-stage and points at itself.
example: Philippians 4:13 — you stride in centre-stage, fist on your chest, first person: I can do.
clear: Centre-stage posture and a chest thump are a manner of arriving, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and nothing from the peg table.

arrive: You slide in sideways along the very edge of the scene, arms folded, and stay there, because the action belongs to someone else: a third figure in the middle whom you nod towards. You watch him; you are not him.
decode: You on the edge, nodding at someone else in the middle = a third person: He.
contrast: I is centre-stage thumping its own chest; He hugs the edge and nods at another figure.
example: Psalm 91:1 — you edge in at the side, arms folded, nodding at the one in the middle of the scene: He that dwelleth.
clear: Edging in sideways and watching is posture, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and nothing from the peg table.

entrance: Slam down from above, this instant
arrive: No approach, no lead-up: you plummet straight down out of nowhere and slam into the middle of the scene with a thump that makes all three pegs jump. One second you were not here; this second you are.
decode: No approach at all, just a sudden slam-landing = this instant: Now.
contrast: Open has you already standing there, unmoving, when the scene begins; Now slams in with a thump everyone hears.
example: Hebrews 11:1 — you drop in from above and land with a thump among the pegs: Now faith is.
clear: A sudden drop and landing is motion, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and no foot or feet are drawn.

entrance: Shoved in from behind, stumbling forward
arrive: A hard shove straight out of the last scene hits you in the back and you stumble in forward, arms windmilling, facing away from where you came, carried by the push. You did not choose this scene; the last one sent you here.
decode: Pushed here by what came before = you are its result: So / Therefore.
contrast: For backs in facing the last scene and points at it; So is propelled in facing away from it, the last scene at its back and no pointing.
example: Genesis 1:27 — a shove straight out of 1:26 sends you stumbling in among the pegs: So God created; Romans 5:1 — the same shove, out of chapter 4: Therefore being justified.
clear: Being shoved and stumbling is motion, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and nothing from the peg table.

arrive: There is no crossing. The scene snaps on and you are simply already in the middle of it, perfectly still, as if you had always been there. Nobody saw you come in, because you did not.
decode: No entrance at all, nothing before the scene = no little word before the first heavy one; the verse starts straight on it: open.
contrast: And is always mid-step with the last scene at your back; open never moved and has no last scene behind it.
example: John 11:35 — no crossing, the scene snaps on and you are already standing in it: Jesus wept; Matthew 5:3 — the same, already there: Blessed are the.
clear: Standing still with no entrance is a posture, not an object; no door, no chain or link, and nothing from the peg table.
